A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 18-page CodeChemist paper, including Appendices A–D. Complete text comparison and rendered-page inspection establish matching scientific content, with no material reading gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original code-generation experiments on MultiPL-HumanEval, MultiPL-MBPP, and Ag-LiveCodeBench-X, plus ablations and supplementary experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original benchmark results, ablations, efficiency measurements, and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain identical hedged sampling, execution/AST uncertainty estimation, adaptive selection, cross-language oracle construction, and scoring procedures. The appendix adaptations are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain the same benchmarks and Lua/C++/Java evaluations, Julia/R extensions, C++-to-Rust experiment, and RepoClassBench Task 56 case study in Appendix B.5.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain Vanilla, majority voting, LLM Judge, Self-Debugging, and S*. Appendix B.4 retains CodeT and MBR-Exec in Table 8. Comparator membership is unchanged within each comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and the appendices retain identical benchmark sizes, model configurations, metrics, sampling budgets, temperatures, clustering thresholds, and experimental procedures.

E4.justification: The sampling, oracle-generation, and adaptive-selection ablations are identical. Hyperparameter, efficiency, generalization, code-style, and failure analyses in Appendices B–C are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix B.1 identically reports five full evaluations with different random seeds and paired t-tests against Vanilla, with p-values below 0.05. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results, and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, CodeChemist's Qwen-1.5B Lua Pass@1 remains 57.8 in Table 1, and its DeepSeek-V3 Lua score remains 50.5 in Table 2.

T1.justification: The problem definition and Equations (1)–(4), including the uncertainty indicator and oracle-based scoring, are identical. Neither version contains additional theorem or proof material.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about training-free functional knowledge transfer, adaptive test-time scaling, and effectiveness across low-resource and complex-syntax programming languages.

C2.justification: Results interpretations and mechanism explanations are identical. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning language-specific behavior, difficult source-language problems, and limited repository-level validation; Appendix C's failure interpretation is unchanged.

D1.justification: Hardware, inference framework, hyperparameters, cross-language normalization rules in Appendix A.2, prompts in Appendix D, and code-access information are identical.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations throughout the paper, and the reference list are identical. Positioning relative to training-based transfer and existing test-time scaling methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 22 June 2026 to v3 dated 5 August 2026. PDF title metadata is aligned with the unchanged displayed title. Body wording, headings, and document structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–4, Tables 1–13, Algorithm 1, prompt boxes, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–18 are pixel-identical; page 1 differs only in the administrative arXiv stamp.

improvement.justification: The scientific text, results, appendices, and substantive presentation are identical. Updating the arXiv stamp and aligning title metadata does not meaningfully change the paper's evidential support, clarity, or reproducibility.
